subject: Re: MAP & environment handoff — network/IP/VPC steps and timeline

Subject: POC MAP request + network info we need

Hi Olga —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Sarah and I spoke internally and we want to lock down the MAP so we can start provisioning network access. Can you share a short checklist for the POC handoff (API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, VPC peering) and a proposed close timeline? Our security team will need the routing and CIDR details to start their review.

Quick Qs:
- Do you require a dedicated org for the POC or can we use a sub-org under our main account?
- Any special keys/roles we should create ahead of time?

Security contact: security@acmehealth.com (cc'd). Looking to start as early as 11/8 if timelines line up.

Thanks,
Alex
Senior Engineer, Acme Health

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <aw@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Sarah Hale <sarah.hale@acmehealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-22 12:03 -0700
Subject: Re: POC MAP request + network info we need

Alex —

Appreciate the quick follow-up. I attached an editable MAP (redwood-map-draft-v2.xlsx) that maps milestones to owners and dates. High level summary here so your security and infra teams have what they need to start:

1) Org & Access
- We recommend a dedicated POC org under your account for isolation. If you prefer a sub-org, we'll note it in the MAP but isolation reduces blast radius.
- Required: one service account for API consumption + one human admin as org owner. We'll provide an RBAC template in the sheet.

2) API keys & service accounts
- We'll provision a scoped API key for the POC (non-prod restrictions). Please confirm the admin email that receives the key secure delivery.

3) IP allowlist
- Provide your egress IP ranges (CIDR) for our allowlist. Minimum: management/control plane and any egress for callbacks.

4) VPC peering
- We support standard VPC peering or PrivateLink-style peering depending on cloud. Marcus can propose the exact steps; I've cc'd him. Attached is a short peering template we typically send to network teams (vpc-peering-template.txt).

5) Timeline & cutover
- Proposed MAP: 3 weeks from kick-off to evaluation handoff, with checkpoints at day 3 (network ready), day 10 (first runs), day 20 (quality/metrics review). Soojin, can you confirm commercial hold and credits?

Next steps:
- Alex: share CIDR blocks and preferred maintenance windows for peering.
- Security: any particular evidence they need (SOC2 section, audit log retention)?
- We'll schedule a 30m sync once we have CIDR to confirm peering approach.

Thanks — sending the MAP now.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Principal AM, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com

[Attachment: redwood-map-draft-v2.xlsx]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <aw@acmehealth.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Sarah Hale <sarah.hale@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-23 08:41 -0700
Subject: Re: POC MAP request + network info we need

Alex / Olga —

Adding a short technical checklist for your network folks. I've also pasted the core items into the vpc-peering-template.txt (attached). For the POC we typically do the following (order matters):

- Confirm CIDRs: provide the customer VPC CIDR(s) + preferred peering VPC CIDR.
- Decide peering mode: route-based peering (standard) vs PrivateLink/GPEN (if you need managed endpoints). PrivateLink reduces cross-VPC routing changes but requires endpoint services.
- Add Redwood service IP ranges to your allowlist (we'll provide a stable list for the POC window).
- Create an IAM role/service account with least-privilege for the POC API key provisioning. We can accept a temporary key or do asymmetric key exchange depending on your org policies.
- If you want KV-cache persistence or large model checkpoints, confirm S3/GCS bucket access (we can mount read-only endpoints).

Operational notes:
- Our typical peering window is a 4-hour maintenance block to validate routing; please confirm a window the week of 11/1–11/8.
- If your net team wants, we can run a dry-run with route tables only (no live traffic).

Happy to run through the vpc template with your network lead — propose Tue 10/26 10:00 PT for a 30m tech sync.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Eng, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: vpc-peering-template.txt]

Alex —

Confirming commercial side: we can reserve a small Dedicated slot and issue a $5k trial credit for the 3-week MAP. We typically hold a capacity reservation for 30 days with an option to convert to a committed Dedicated plan if you expand.

Proposed milestone dates (reflecting Olga's MAP draft):
- Day 0 (kickoff): finalize CIDR + sign MAP
- Day 3: IP allowlist + API key delivery
- Day 10: baseline evaluation runs (your first 1k requests)
- Day 20: quality review & cost estimates for scale

Please let us know if you need a PO or a short SOW to accompany the MAP for internal approvals. I can start the DocuSign if you approve the MAP draft.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Lead Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
